Getting started with anndata.claude

Source: vignettes/anndata-claude.Rmd
anndata-claude.Rmd

anndata.claude is an R port of Python anndata. Its first priority is that .h5ad files round trip between R and Python.

library(anndata.claude)

Create an AnnData

An AnnData holds a matrix X with observations (obs) as rows and variables (var) as columns.

X <- matrix(as.numeric(1:12), nrow = 3)
obs <- data.frame(
  cell_type = c("T", "B", "T"),
  row.names = c("cell1", "cell2", "cell3")
)
var <- data.frame(
  highly_variable = c(TRUE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE),
  row.names = c("gene1", "gene2", "gene3", "gene4")
)
adata <- AnnData(X, obs = obs, var = var)
adata
#> AnnData object with n_obs × n_vars = 3 × 4
#>     obs: 'cell_type'
#>     var: 'highly_variable'
#>     layers: None (.X)

Assign Slots

Annotations are aligned to obs or var and are kept in obsm, varm, obsp, varp and layers. Unstructured data goes in uns.

adata$obsm[["pca"]] <- matrix(c(0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 1, 2, 3), nrow = 3)
adata$layers[["counts"]] <- X * 2
adata$uns[["note"]] <- "example"
adata$obs[["batch"]] <- c("a", "a", "b")
adata
#> AnnData object with n_obs × n_vars = 3 × 4
#>     obs: 'cell_type', 'batch'
#>     var: 'highly_variable'
#>     uns: 'note'
#>     obsm: 'pca'
#>     layers: 'counts', None (.X)

Subset

Indexing is 1-based, and negative indices exclude.

adata[1:2, ]
#> View of AnnData object with n_obs × n_vars = 2 × 4
#>     obs: 'cell_type', 'batch'
#>     var: 'highly_variable'
#>     uns: 'note'
#>     obsm: 'pca'
#>     layers: 'counts', None (.X)
adata[-1, c("gene1", "gene3")]$shape
#> [1] 2 2

Subsetting returns a View, which shares data with the original AnnData and prints with a View of prefix. Modifying a View makes it an independent object and leaves the original unchanged, with a warning.

sub <- adata[1:2, ]
sub$is_view
#> [1] TRUE
sub$obs[["batch"]] <- c("x", "y")
#> Warning: Trying to modify attribute `.obs` of view, initializing view as
#> actual.
sub$is_view
#> [1] FALSE
adata$obs[["batch"]]
#> [1] "a" "a" "b"

Values extracted from a View are plain R objects, so unlike Python x <- sub$X; x[1, 1] <- 0 does not change the View. Assign through the View (sub$X[1, 1] <- 0) instead. This and the other differences from Python are listed in vignette("deviations").

Write and read h5ad 

path <- tempfile(fileext = ".h5ad")
write_h5ad(adata, path)
roundtrip <- read_h5ad(path)
roundtrip
#> AnnData object with n_obs × n_vars = 3 × 4
#>     obs: 'cell_type', 'batch'
#>     var: 'highly_variable'
#>     uns: 'note'
#>     obsm: 'pca'
#>     layers: 'counts', None (.X)
identical(roundtrip$obs_names, adata$obs_names)
#> [1] TRUE

Use compression = "gzip" to compress datasets, and as_sparse in read_h5ad() to read a dense X as a sparse matrix.

Backed mode

read_h5ad(backed = "r") keeps X (and raw$X) on disk and reads only the parts that are indexed. Everything else is read into memory. Use backed = "r+" to write changes to X back to the file.

backed <- read_h5ad(path, backed = "r")
backed$isbacked
#> [1] TRUE
backed$filename
#> [1] "/tmp/Rtmpyik04p/file1d652cb8ab00.h5ad"
backed$X[1:2, c(1, 3)]
#>      [,1] [,2]
#> [1,]    1    7
#> [2,]    2    8

chunked_X() visits the rows of X in chunks and chunk_X() returns random or chosen rows.

chunks <- backed$chunked_X(2)
length(chunks)
#> [1] 2
chunks[[2]]$start
#> [1] 3
backed$chunk_X(I(3))
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4]
#> [1,]    3    6    9   12

to_memory() loads the whole object and write_h5ad() or copy(filename) write a backed object to a new file. Assigning X ends backed mode, and the file is left unchanged.

in_memory <- backed$to_memory()
in_memory$isbacked
#> [1] FALSE
backed$file$close()

sparse_dataset() makes a handle on a sparse matrix in an open rhdf5 group, which also has $append() to add rows or columns on disk.

Move a file to Python and back

The file written above can be read by Python anndata directly. These chunks need Python so they are shown but not run.

import anndata as ad

adata = ad.read_h5ad("example.h5ad")
adata.obs["from_python"] = True
adata.write_h5ad("from-python.h5ad")
back <- read_h5ad("from-python.h5ad")
back$obs[["from_python"]]

Write and read zarr

write_zarr() writes a zarr v3 store (a directory) and read_zarr() reads v3 and v2 stores.

zarr_path <- tempfile(fileext = ".zarr")
write_zarr(adata, zarr_path)
zarr_roundtrip <- read_zarr(zarr_path)
zarr_roundtrip
#> AnnData object with n_obs × n_vars = 3 × 4
#>     obs: 'cell_type', 'batch'
#>     var: 'highly_variable'
#>     uns: 'note'
#>     obsm: 'pca'
#>     layers: 'counts', None (.X)
identical(zarr_roundtrip$obs_names, adata$obs_names)
#> [1] TRUE

Use the compressors argument to choose the compression (zstd, gzip, blosc or none) and shards to set the shard shape. Writing zarr v2 is not yet supported.

Lazy reading

read_lazy() reads an h5ad file or zarr store into an AnnData whose X, layers, mappings, obs and var are lazy. Arrays are DelayedArrays (sparse ones stay sparse) and data frame columns are read when they are used. uns is read into memory.

lazy <- read_lazy(zarr_path)
class(lazy$X)
#> [1] "DelayedMatrix"
#> attr(,"package")
#> [1] "DelayedArray"
lazy$X[1:2, ]
#> <2 x 4> DelayedMatrix object of type "double":
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4]
#> [1,]    1    4    7   10
#> [2,]    2    5    8   11

Subsetting, Views, copy() and t() stay lazy, and to_memory() reads everything. Writing a lazy object is not supported yet, so call to_memory() first.

lazy_memory <- lazy$to_memory()
class(lazy_memory$X)
#> [1] "matrix" "array"

read_elem_lazy() does the same for a single Element, and chunks sets the chunk shape of the DelayedArray grid.

read_elem_lazy(zarr_path, "X", chunks = c(2, NA))
#> <3 x 4> DelayedMatrix object of type "double":
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4]
#> [1,]    1    4    7   10
#> [2,]    2    5    8   11
#> [3,]    3    6    9   12

Concatenate

concat() combines AnnData objects along axis ("obs" by default) and follows Python’s concat(). An inner join keeps the variables every object has and an outer join keeps all of them, filling new entries with fill_value.

a <- AnnData(
  matrix(1, nrow = 2, ncol = 2),
  obs = data.frame(row.names = c("a1", "a2")),
  var = data.frame(row.names = c("g1", "g2"))
)
b <- AnnData(
  matrix(2, nrow = 2, ncol = 2),
  obs = data.frame(row.names = c("b1", "b2")),
  var = data.frame(row.names = c("g2", "g3"))
)
concat(list(a, b))$var_names
#> [1] "g2"
concat(list(a, b), join = "outer")$X
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3]
#> [1,]    1    1   NA
#> [2,]    1    1   NA
#> [3,]   NA    2    2
#> [4,]   NA    2    2

A named list gives the keys, which label stores in obs and index_unique adds to the names.

combined <- concat(
  list(first = a, second = b),
  label = "batch",
  index_unique = "-"
)
combined$obs
#> DataFrame with 4 rows and 1 column
#>              batch
#>           <factor>
#> a1-first    first 
#> a2-first    first 
#> b1-second   second
#> b2-second   second

merge and uns_merge choose which annotations of the other axis and which uns entries are kept ("same", "unique", "first" or "only", or a function). Views and backed objects can be concatenated, and objects from read_lazy() give a lazy result.

Other formats

read_text() and read_csv() read delimited text, from a path or a character vector of lines. The first column holds the obs names when it is not numeric and dtype (default "float32") sets the type of X.

lines <- c("cell,g1,g2", "c1,1,2", "c2,3,4")
read_csv(lines)$to_df()
#>    g1 g2
#> c1  1  2
#> c2  3  4

read_mtx() (Matrix Market), read_umi_tools(), read_hdf() and read_excel() (needs readxl) read other sources, and all return an AnnData. read_umi_tools() gives a sparse X with sorted names.

path <- tempfile(fileext = ".tsv")
writeLines(
  c("gene\tcell\tcount", "g2\tc2\t3", "g1\tc1\t1", "g3\tc1\t2"),
  path
)
read_umi_tools(path)
#> AnnData object with n_obs × n_vars = 2 × 3
#>     layers: None (.X)

write_csvs() writes obs, var, obsm, varm and uns (and X with skip_data = FALSE) as csv files that pandas reads the same as Python’s output.

dir <- tempfile("csvs")
write_csvs(adata, dir)
list.files(dir, recursive = TRUE)
#> [1] "obs.csv"      "obsm.csv"     "uns/note.csv" "var.csv"      "varm.csv"
unlink(dir, recursive = TRUE)

Move a zarr store to Python and back

Python anndata reads and writes the same store. These chunks need Python so they are shown but not run.

import anndata as ad

adata = ad.read_zarr("example.zarr")
adata.obs["from_python"] = True
adata.write_zarr("from-python.zarr")
back <- read_zarr("from-python.zarr")
back$obs[["from_python"]]
